opex.name: Technology and infrastructure
opex.note: Running and expanding the platform: data-center operations and the engineering behind the AI cloud; up from $561M a year ago as capacity grew.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling the cloud to AI labs, hyperscalers and large enterprises; up from $11M a year ago as the sales effort scaled.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office: finance, legal and company-wide administration.

follow100Note: The striking thing: interest and other non-operating costs took $24.64 of every $100 — and running the platform took another $61.26. The business lost $35.61 of every $100 it took in.
footerNote: Gross profit = revenue less cost of revenue. The $740M net loss is drawn as 'Covered by cash on hand'.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted net loss per share, vs -$1.49 a year ago

kpis.label: Capex
kpis.note: purchases of property and equipment in Q1 alone

oneTimers: Stock-based compensation of $153M is stripped out of the adjusted figures: the non-GAAP reconciliation removes $153M of stock-based compensation, $11M of amortization of acquired intangibles and $1M of acquisition-related costs on the way from the GAAP net loss of $740M to the adjusted net loss of $589M. There was no fair-value gain or loss this quarter.
otherDetail: Net non-operating expense of $512M: interest expense, net was $536M — the cost of borrowing heavily to build data centers — partly offset by $24M of other income, net. There was no fair-value gain or loss this quarter.

segments.name: AI cloud infrastructure
segments.note: Renting out GPU-powered cloud capacity purpose-built for AI training and inference (running trained models); the company's single revenue line, up 112% YoY as demand from AI labs, hyperscalers and enterprises surged.

takeaways.text: Revenue hit $2,078M, up from $982M a year ago, and the revenue backlog — work customers have committed to — reached about $99.4B at quarter-end, with new Meta and Anthropic agreements signed in the quarter.
takeaways.title: Revenue more than doubled

takeaways.text: Operations lost $144M, but net interest expense was $536M. After $24M of other income and $84M of tax, the net loss was $740M — the price of borrowing to build ahead of demand.
takeaways.title: Interest is what makes the loss bigger

takeaways.text: CoreWeave spent $7,695M on property and equipment in the quarter — about 3.7 times its revenue — while operating cash flow was $2,984M. Active power passed 1 GW, with over 3.5 GW contracted.
takeaways.title: Spending to build is enormous

verdict: CoreWeave's revenue more than doubled to $2.1B and its backlog reached $99.4B, but $536M of net interest turned a $144M operating loss into a $740M net loss.
